summary: Forestry tower on Mount Jamieson (Kamiskotia), west of Timmins, later planned as a joint radar and forestry tower; SooToday calls the remains a communications node.

corrections.why: The 1959-1960 reports and the SooToday column use Kamiskotia and Mount Jamieson; 'Kamistokia' appears in none of the sources read. A reviewer should choose the final name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kamiskotia is the spelling in the 1959-1960 reports and in SooToday; the record's 'Kamistokia' is a different spelling. The hill is also called Mount Jamieson in the reports, which is not the same as Jamieson's Mountain in Renfrew County.

notes_for_editor: The 1959-1961 Gap Filler memos are the strongest evidence; they are reproductions on candemuseum.org of National Archives of Canada records, so check the original file references before publication if possible. Open points: (1) the 1959 report says the fire destroyed the forestry tower yet also describes Dan McCrory occupying it, while the 1960 survey describes a standing 80 ft tower on the summit and does not mention any loss; the story reports both and says the record is unclear. (2) No source read says whether the 1961 joint radar and forestry tower was built, or whether the Ontario tower was removed as proposed. The SooToday caption says 'the original fire tower' is now atop the ski hill, which may mean the proposal was not carried out; this is not stated outright. (3) Resort name conflict: Firelookout says Kamiskotia Snow Resort, SooToday says the resort was rebranded Mount Jamieson Resort. (4) Access is not stated in any source read; the story advises against climbing because the tower is now a communications node. (5) A search snippet mentions the Timmins Ski Club moving to Mount Jamieson in 1945 and the Kreiner family's development of the hill; those pages were not read and are not used. (6) The sootoday photo of the tower has no licence stated, so no photo is listed. (7) The Treasury Board approval is dated 29 Sep 1960 in the May 1961 memo and 24 Sep 1960 in the September 1961 memo; the story gives both dates and does not choose one.
